This is distinct from endometriosis, which refers to ectopic endometrial tissue outside the uterus entirely (e.g., ovaries, peritoneum), even though both conditions involve displaced endometrial tissue responding to hormonal cycling.

incorrectas.A: Leiomyoma (fibroid) is a benign smooth muscle tumor of the myometrium, a distinct clonal neoplastic proliferation rather than ectopic endometrial glands and stroma infiltrating the muscle, so it does not match the description in the question.
incorrectas.C: Endometrial hyperplasia refers to excessive proliferation of the endometrial lining itself within the uterine cavity, driven by unopposed estrogen, not ectopic glandular/stromal tissue within the myometrium as described in adenomyosis.
incorrectas.D: An endocervical polyp is a localized benign growth of endocervical glandular tissue projecting into the endocervical canal, unrelated to ectopic endometrial tissue embedded within the myometrium, which is the defining feature of adenomyosis.

preguntas.q: Continuous (non-pulsatile) administration of which hormone class can be used medically to treat adenomyosis by suppressing gonadotropin release?

e.correcta: GnRH is normally released in a pulsatile fashion, which is required to stimulate pituitary gonadotrope receptors and drive LH/FSH secretion; continuous, non-pulsatile GnRH agonist administration instead causes receptor downregulation and desensitization, paradoxically suppressing gonadotropin release. This creates a hypoestrogenic state that shrinks estrogen-dependent tissue such as ectopic endometrial glands in adenomyosis, providing symptomatic relief, though it is typically used short-term due to menopause-like side effects (e.g., bone loss).

incorrectas.A: Estrogen itself would stimulate rather than suppress gonadotropin-dependent endometrial tissue and is not used therapeutically to treat adenomyosis; it would worsen the estrogen-driven proliferation underlying the disease.
incorrectas.C: Progesterone antagonists (like mifepristone) work by blocking progesterone receptors, a different mechanism entirely from suppressing GnRH/gonadotropin pulsatility, and are not the classic answer for this mechanism-based question.
incorrectas.D: Androgen receptor blockers act on androgen signaling pathways and have no established role in suppressing gonadotropin release or treating adenomyosis via this pulsatility mechanism.

preguntas.q: Sites of endometriosis, especially in the ovary, carry an increased long-term risk of developing what?

e.correcta: Ectopic endometrial tissue in endometriosis, particularly within ovarian endometriomas ('chocolate cysts'), undergoes chronic hormonally-driven cyclical proliferation and bleeding, and this persistent tissue can accumulate the genetic alterations (e.g., ARID1A mutations) that predispose to malignant transformation — most notably endometrioid and clear cell ovarian carcinoma. This link is why long-standing ovarian endometriomas warrant surveillance for concerning changes such as rapid growth or solid components.

incorrectas.B: Tuberculosis of the pelvis is an infectious process typically arising from hematogenous spread from pulmonary TB, unrelated to the hormonally responsive ectopic endometrial tissue seen in endometriosis.
incorrectas.C: Pelvic inflammatory disease is an ascending infection usually from sexually transmitted organisms (e.g., Chlamydia, Neisseria gonorrhoeae), a distinct infectious etiology rather than a long-term neoplastic consequence of endometriosis.
incorrectas.D: Uterine prolapse results from weakening of pelvic floor support structures (often from childbirth trauma or aging), a structural/mechanical problem unrelated to the malignant potential of ectopic endometrial implants.

preguntas.q: A condition defined by proliferation of endometrial glands out of proportion to the surrounding stroma is called what?

e.correcta: Endometrial hyperplasia is defined precisely by an increase in the gland-to-stroma ratio, driven by unopposed estrogen stimulation of the endometrium without the counterbalancing secretory/differentiating effect of progesterone. This occurs classically in obesity (peripheral aromatization of androgens), PCOS (chronic anovulation), estrogen-secreting tumors, and unopposed estrogen replacement therapy. The clinical importance is that hyperplasia, especially with cytologic atypia, is the precursor lesion to endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, so it is worked up with endometrial biopsy in women with abnormal uterine bleeding.

incorrectas.B: An endometrial polyp is a localized, often pedunculated overgrowth of endometrial tissue (glands and fibrous stroma) projecting into the uterine cavity, not a diffuse process defined by an altered gland-to-stroma ratio throughout the endometrium.
incorrectas.C: Adenomyosis is the presence of endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium (the muscular wall), causing an enlarged, boggy, tender uterus — it is a problem of ectopic location, not of glandular proliferation outpacing stroma within the endometrium itself.
incorrectas.D: Endometrial carcinoma is the malignant transformation of endometrial glands with invasive growth beyond the basement membrane; hyperplasia is the premalignant precursor state that precedes it but does not yet show malignant invasion.

preguntas.q: Endometrial hyperplasia typically presents with abnormal uterine bleeding occurring in which clinical context?

e.correcta: Endometrial hyperplasia results from unopposed estrogen stimulation of the endometrium without the balancing effect of progesterone, a scenario that is common after menopause when anovulatory cycles and peripheral aromatization of androgens (especially in obese patients) provide estrogen without a corpus luteum to produce progesterone. Because postmenopausal women should not have any uterine bleeding, any bleeding in this population is considered abnormal and endometrial hyperplasia (or carcinoma) must be excluded first.

incorrectas.A: While anovulatory cycles can cause unopposed estrogen and hyperplasia in premenopausal women too, the classic and highest-yield clinical context emphasized for endometrial hyperplasia is postmenopausal bleeding, since any bleeding after menopause is presumed pathologic until proven otherwise.
incorrectas.C: Hyperplasia is not linked to pregnancy; pregnancy is a high-progesterone state that would not produce the estrogen-driven overgrowth seen in hyperplasia.
incorrectas.D: Adolescence is associated with anovulatory cycles from an immature hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, but hyperplasia as a distinct diagnosis with malignant potential is not the classic presentation taught for this age group.

preguntas.q: Endometrial hyperplasia is histologically classified based on architectural growth pattern (simple vs. complex) and the presence or absence of which additional feature?

o.C: Mitotic rate greater than 50 per high-power field

e.correcta: Endometrial hyperplasia classification incorporates both the architectural pattern (simple vs. complex, referring to gland crowding and complexity) and, critically, the presence or absence of cellular (cytologic) atypia, because atypia is the strongest predictor of progression to endometrial carcinoma. Hyperplasia with atypia carries a substantially higher risk of coexisting or progressing to carcinoma than hyperplasia without atypia, which is why this feature drives management decisions (surveillance/progestin therapy vs. hysterectomy).

incorrectas.A: Vascular invasion is a feature assessed in established carcinoma to determine staging and risk of metastasis, not a criterion used to subclassify hyperplasia, which is a preinvasive, non-malignant proliferative process.
incorrectas.C: A specific mitotic rate cutoff like 50 per high-power field is not part of the standard architectural/atypia-based classification scheme for endometrial hyperplasia; grading here depends on gland pattern and nuclear atypia, not a quantitative mitotic count threshold.
incorrectas.D: Necrosis is a feature more typical of invasive or high-grade malignant lesions and is not a defining criterion in the simple/complex, with/without atypia classification system used for endometrial hyperplasia.

preguntas.q: Among the histologic features of endometrial hyperplasia, which is the most important predictor of progression to carcinoma?

e.correcta: Cellular (cytologic) atypia — irregular nuclear size, shape, and chromatin pattern — reflects genetic instability in the glandular epithelial cells themselves and is the strongest histologic predictor of progression to endometrial carcinoma, far more so than architectural crowding alone. This is why the modern classification system distinguishes hyperplasia with atypia (high risk, often managed with hysterectomy) from hyperplasia without atypia (lower risk, often managed with progestins).

incorrectas.A: A simple (as opposed to complex) architectural pattern refers to gland shape and crowding, but architecture alone is a weaker predictor of malignant progression than the presence of cytologic atypia.
incorrectas.C: Plasma cells are markers of chronic endometritis (inflammation), not hyperplasia progression, and are not part of the atypia/architecture grading scheme used to predict carcinoma risk.
incorrectas.D: Gland-to-stroma ratio reflects architectural complexity but, like architecture alone, is less predictive of malignant transformation than cytologic atypia, which is why atypia is singled out as the key prognostic feature.

preguntas.q: Between simple and complex architectural patterns of endometrial hyperplasia, which carries a higher risk of progression to carcinoma?

e.correcta: Complex endometrial hyperplasia (increased gland crowding and complexity of glandular architecture) carries a higher risk of progression to endometrial carcinoma than simple hyperplasia, and this risk rises further when cytologic atypia is present. The architectural complexity reflects a greater degree of disordered, crowded proliferation driven by unopposed estrogen, which more closely approximates the histology seen in early carcinoma than the more orderly simple hyperplasia pattern.

incorrectas.A: Simple hyperplasia shows less glandular crowding and architectural distortion than complex hyperplasia, and carries a substantially lower risk of progressing to carcinoma, making it the lower-risk end of the hyperplasia spectrum rather than the higher-risk one.
incorrectas.C: The two patterns do not carry identical risk — complex architecture (especially with atypia) is associated with meaningfully higher rates of progression to carcinoma than simple hyperplasia, which is why grading hyperplasia by architecture and atypia matters clinically.
incorrectas.D: Both simple and complex hyperplasia carry some risk of progression to carcinoma (higher with atypia), so it is incorrect to say neither progresses — untreated atypical hyperplasia in particular has a well-documented risk of evolving into endometrioid adenocarcinoma.

preguntas.q: Endometrial hyperplasia, particularly when accompanied by cellular atypia, carries an increased risk of progression to which condition?

e.correcta: Endometrial hyperplasia, particularly with atypia, represents a step along the estrogen-driven (Type I) pathway to endometrial carcinoma, where persistent unopposed estrogen stimulation causes progressively atypical glandular proliferation that can accumulate additional mutations (e.g., PTEN) and progress to endometrioid adenocarcinoma. Recognizing hyperplasia with atypia as a true precursor lesion is why it is treated aggressively (progestin therapy or hysterectomy) to prevent this progression.

incorrectas.B: Cervical carcinoma arises from cervical squamous or glandular epithelium via an HPV-driven pathway, an entirely separate mechanism from endometrial glandular hyperplasia and estrogen exposure.
incorrectas.C: Ovarian teratomas are germ cell tumors arising from totipotent germ cells, unrelated to endometrial glandular hyperplasia or estrogen-driven proliferation.
incorrectas.D: Vulvar carcinoma arises from vulvar squamous epithelium, often via HPV or chronic dermatologic conditions (e.g., lichen sclerosus), not from endometrial hyperplasia.

preguntas.q: What is the most common invasive (malignant) carcinoma of the female genital tract?

e.correcta: Endometrial carcinoma is the most common invasive malignancy of the female genital tract overall, typically arising from unopposed estrogen-driven endometrial hyperplasia that progresses to endometrioid adenocarcinoma, and presenting early with postmenopausal bleeding that prompts biopsy before extensive local invasion. Because it is symptomatic early and thus often caught while still confined to the uterus, it accounts for the highest incidence of invasive gynecologic cancer even though it is not the most lethal. This distinction between "most common" (endometrial) and "most lethal" (ovarian) is a frequently tested contrast.

incorrectas.A: Cervical carcinoma, once the leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality, has declined significantly in incidence due to HPV vaccination and Pap smear screening, making it less common than endometrial carcinoma in current epidemiology.
incorrectas.C: Vulvar carcinoma is a much rarer squamous cell malignancy, usually related to either HPV infection or chronic lichen sclerosus, and does not approach the incidence of endometrial carcinoma.
incorrectas.D: Vaginal carcinoma is the rarest of the gynecologic malignancies, often representing metastatic or contiguous spread from cervical cancer rather than a common primary invasive tumor.

preguntas.q: In approximately 25% of endometrial carcinoma cases, the tumor arises in an atrophic endometrium without any identifiable precursor lesion. This is known as which pathway?

e.correcta: The sporadic pathway (Type II) accounts for roughly 25% of endometrial carcinomas and arises in an atrophic, estrogen-independent endometrium without passing through a hyperplasia precursor stage, typically in older postmenopausal women. These tumors are more aggressive (often serous or clear cell histology) and are driven by different genetic alterations, classically p53 mutations, rather than the estrogen-hyperplasia sequence seen in Type I disease.

incorrectas.A: The estrogen-dependent (Type I) pathway is the more common (~75%) route and specifically requires a hyperplasia precursor arising from unopposed estrogen stimulation — the opposite of the atrophic, precursor-free presentation described in the question.
incorrectas.C: Lynch syndrome is a specific hereditary cause of endometrial (and colon) cancer due to mismatch repair gene mutations, but it is not synonymous with the general sporadic, non-precursor pathway described here.
incorrectas.D: HPV-mediated carcinogenesis is the mechanism for cervical cancer, not endometrial carcinoma, which is not related to HPV infection.

preguntas.q: A malignant proliferation of endometrial glands with invasive potential is termed what?

e.correcta: Endometrial carcinoma is defined by malignant transformation of endometrial glandular epithelium with the capacity to invade the myometrium and, eventually, metastasize — the features that separate cancer from benign proliferative endometrial disease. It typically arises through two pathways: an estrogen-driven route progressing through atypical hyperplasia (endometrioid histology), or a p53-mutated pathway arising in atrophic endometrium (serous histology) in older women. Recognizing invasive potential is what makes this the answer, since none of the other listed entities can invade or metastasize.

incorrectas.B: Endometrial hyperplasia is excessive glandular proliferation, often from unopposed estrogen, and it is a precursor lesion — atypical hyperplasia in particular carries malignant potential — but by definition it has not yet acquired invasive capability, which is what the question specifies.
incorrectas.A: An endometrial polyp is a localized benign overgrowth of endometrial stroma and glands projecting into the uterine cavity; it can cause abnormal bleeding but does not invade underlying tissue and only rarely harbors malignant foci.
incorrectas.D: Adenomyosis is the presence of endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium itself, causing an enlarged, boggy uterus with dysmenorrhea/menorrhagia — this represents ectopic benign tissue, not a malignant, invasive glandular proliferation.

preguntas.q: Endometrial carcinoma most classically presents with bleeding occurring in which clinical setting?

e.correcta: Endometrial carcinoma classically presents with postmenopausal bleeding because the tumor arises from endometrial glandular tissue that outgrows its blood supply and sheds abnormally, and because postmenopausal women should have no uterine bleeding at baseline, any bleeding prompts immediate endometrial biopsy to rule out malignancy. This is why endometrial carcinoma is often caught at an early, more curable stage compared to cancers that lack an early warning sign.

incorrectas.A: Premenarchal bleeding (before puberty) is abnormal for entirely different reasons (e.g., precocious puberty, foreign body, trauma) and is not the classic presentation of endometrial carcinoma, a disease of older, typically postmenopausal women.
incorrectas.C: Mid-cycle spotting is usually a benign, self-limited finding related to the estrogen dip at ovulation in premenopausal women, not the presentation of endometrial malignancy.
incorrectas.D: Bleeding during pregnancy has an entirely different differential (e.g., placental abruption, previa, miscarriage) and is not related to endometrial carcinoma, which occurs in a non-gravid, typically atrophic or hyperplastic endometrium.

preguntas.q: Endometrial carcinoma is classically described as arising via two distinct pathogenic pathways. Which two pathways are these?

o.C: Lynch syndrome pathway and BRCA pathway

e.correcta: Endometrial carcinoma is classically divided into the hyperplasia (Type I, estrogen-dependent) pathway, in which unopposed estrogen drives endometrial hyperplasia that progresses to typically endometrioid, lower-grade carcinoma, and the sporadic (Type II) pathway, in which carcinoma arises de novo in atrophic endometrium without a hyperplastic precursor, tends to be higher-grade (serous/clear cell), and is driven by p53 mutations. Distinguishing these two pathways matters because they differ in risk factors, typical age of onset, histology, and prognosis.

incorrectas.B: Adenomyosis and metaplasia are not part of the classic two-pathway model of endometrial carcinogenesis; adenomyosis refers to ectopic endometrial tissue within the myometrium and is a separate, generally benign condition.
incorrectas.C: Lynch syndrome and BRCA are hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes that increase risk of endometrial or other cancers, but they are not themselves named as the two overarching sporadic/hyperplasia pathogenic pathways.
incorrectas.D: HPV-driven and radiation-induced pathways are mechanisms relevant to cervical or other radiation-associated cancers, not the two classic pathways of endometrial carcinogenesis.

preguntas.q: A woman presents with endometrial carcinoma arising through the hyperplasia (estrogen-driven) pathway. What is the average age of presentation for this pathway?

e.correcta: The hyperplasia (Type I, estrogen-driven) pathway to endometrial carcinoma classically presents around age 60, somewhat younger than the sporadic (Type II) pathway, reflecting the cumulative years of unopposed estrogen exposure (from obesity, anovulation, early menarche/late menopause) required to drive the hyperplasia-to-carcinoma sequence. Knowing this age distinction helps distinguish the two pathways clinically, since Type II tumors tend to present in slightly older patients with atrophic, not hyperplastic, endometrium.

incorrectas.A: 40 years is too young for the typical presentation of endometrial carcinoma via either pathway; endometrial carcinoma is overwhelmingly a disease of peri- and postmenopausal women.
incorrectas.B: 50 years is closer to average menopausal age but still younger than the classically cited average age (60) for the estrogen-driven hyperplasia pathway.
incorrectas.D: 70 years is more in line with the slightly older average age attributed to the sporadic (Type II, p53-driven) pathway rather than the hyperplasia pathway described in this question.

preguntas.q: The sporadic pathway of endometrial carcinoma, which is not estrogen-related and exhibits aggressive behavior, has an average age of presentation of approximately how many years?

e.correcta: The sporadic (type II) pathway of endometrial carcinoma is not driven by unopposed estrogen but instead arises from TP53 mutations in a background of endometrial atrophy, producing aggressive serous or clear cell histology, and it classically presents later in life, around age 70, compared to the estrogen-driven (type I) endometrioid pathway that presents in younger, often obese or estrogen-excess patients around their 50s-60s. Recognizing this age and mechanism split is a classic way Step 1 tests understanding of the two distinct endometrial cancer pathways.

incorrectas.A: 50 years is more typical of the estrogen-related (type I, endometrioid) pathway, which occurs in a younger population with risk factors like obesity and unopposed estrogen exposure, not the sporadic TP53-driven pathway.
incorrectas.B: 60 years falls between the two pathways but still underestimates the typically later presentation of the aggressive, non-estrogen-related sporadic pathway, which is classically described as occurring around 70 years old.
incorrectas.D: 80 years overestimates the average presentation age for the sporadic pathway; while it can occur in very elderly patients, the classically cited average age for this pathway is approximately 70, not 80.

preguntas.q: Endometrial carcinoma arising via the sporadic (non-estrogen-related, aggressive) pathway is most commonly associated with mutation of which gene?

e.correcta: The sporadic pathway to endometrial carcinoma is classically associated with p53 mutation, a tumor suppressor gene whose loss of function disables apoptosis and cell cycle checkpoint control, allowing genomically unstable, aggressive tumors (e.g., serous carcinoma) to arise de novo without an estrogen-driven hyperplastic precursor. This contrasts with the more indolent, estrogen-dependent pathway, which is instead associated with PTEN, KRAS, and microsatellite instability/mismatch repair mutations.

incorrectas.A: KRAS mutations are associated with the estrogen-dependent (Type I, hyperplasia) pathway, not the aggressive sporadic pathway described in this question.
incorrectas.B: PTEN mutations (loss of this tumor suppressor that normally restrains PI3K/AKT signaling) are the classic finding in the Type I, estrogen-driven pathway, not the sporadic pathway.
incorrectas.D: APC mutations are classically associated with colorectal carcinogenesis (familial adenomatous polyposis and sporadic colon cancer), not endometrial carcinoma.

preguntas.q: Risk factors for endometrial carcinoma arising via the hyperplasia pathway (early menarche/late menopause, nulliparity, anovulatory cycles, obesity) all share which common underlying mechanism?

e.correcta: Early menarche/late menopause increases the total number of menstrual cycles (and estrogen exposure) over a lifetime, nulliparity removes the estrogen-lowering breaks that pregnancy provides, anovulatory cycles fail to produce a corpus luteum and thus lack the progesterone that normally opposes estrogen's proliferative effect, and obesity increases peripheral aromatization of androgens to estrogen in adipose tissue — all converging on a single mechanism of chronic, unopposed estrogen exposure to the endometrium. This unifying mechanism is exactly why these risk factors drive the Type I hyperplasia-to-carcinoma pathway.

incorrectas.B: Progesterone actually opposes endometrial proliferation (it is protective, which is why it's used therapeutically for hyperplasia), so these risk factors reflect a lack of progesterone's balancing effect rather than chronic progesterone exposure.
incorrectas.C: While obesity does increase peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogen (via aromatase), the unifying downstream driver of endometrial proliferation across all these risk factors is the resulting estrogen exposure, not androgen exposure itself.
incorrectas.D: Prolactin is not implicated in the pathogenesis of endometrial hyperplasia or these classic risk factors; hyperprolactinemia's clinical concern relates to hypogonadism and galactorrhea/amenorrhea, not endometrial proliferation.

preguntas.q: A 45-year-old woman with a strong family history of colon cancer is diagnosed with endometrial carcinoma. Genetic testing reveals a germline mutation in a DNA mismatch repair gene. Which autosomal dominant syndrome, which increases risk of colon, ovarian, and endometrial carcinoma, does she likely have?

e.correcta: Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer, HNPCC) is an autosomal dominant condition caused by germline mutations in DNA mismatch repair genes (e.g., MLH1, MSH2), leading to microsatellite instability and a markedly increased lifetime risk of colorectal cancer as well as extracolonic cancers, most notably endometrial and ovarian carcinoma. The combination of early-onset endometrial cancer with a strong family history of colon cancer and a documented mismatch repair mutation is the classic clinical vignette pointing to this diagnosis.

incorrectas.A: Familial adenomatous polyposis is caused by APC gene mutations leading to hundreds to thousands of colonic polyps and colon cancer, but it is not driven by mismatch repair gene defects and is not the classic cause of synchronous endometrial cancer risk.
incorrectas.B: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome involves STK11 mutations causing hamartomatous GI polyps and mucocutaneous pigmentation, with increased cancer risk at multiple sites, but it is not a mismatch repair disorder and does not match this vignette.
incorrectas.D: Li-Fraumeni syndrome is caused by germline p53 mutations leading to a wide spectrum of early-onset cancers (sarcomas, breast, brain, adrenal), not by mismatch repair gene defects, so it does not fit the genetic finding described.

preguntas.q: What is the most common tumor found in females?

e.correcta: Leiomyoma (uterine fibroid) is the most common tumor in females overall, arising from benign monoclonal proliferation of myometrial smooth muscle cells under estrogen/progesterone influence, which is why fibroids grow during reproductive years and regress after menopause. Their high prevalence (affecting a large proportion of women by mid-life) combined with their benign nature makes them a very commonly tested 'most common tumor' fact distinct from cancer-specific statistics.

incorrectas.A: Ovarian cystadenomas are common benign ovarian tumors, but they are far less prevalent overall in the female population than uterine leiomyomas, which affect a substantially larger proportion of women.
incorrectas.C: Endometrial carcinoma is the most common gynecologic malignancy, but 'most common tumor in females' overall (including benign tumors) is a much broader category won by the far more prevalent, benign leiomyoma, not this cancer.
incorrectas.D: Leiomyosarcoma is a rare, malignant smooth muscle tumor and is actually a distinct and much less common entity than its benign counterpart, leiomyoma — the malignant version is uncommon, not the 'most common tumor' answer.

preguntas.q: Which demographic has an increased incidence of leiomyoma (uterine fibroid), with peak occurrence between 20-40 years old?

e.correcta: Leiomyomas (uterine fibroids) are estrogen- and progesterone-sensitive smooth muscle tumors, and African American women have a markedly higher incidence, often presenting earlier (peak 20-40 years) and with larger or more numerous tumors, likely reflecting a combination of genetic susceptibility and hormonal receptor differences that are still being characterized. This demographic disparity is a testable epidemiologic fact distinguishing fibroid risk from other reproductive tumors.

incorrectas.A: Asian American women do not show the same elevated incidence of leiomyoma seen in African American women; fibroid epidemiology studies consistently rank this group closer to baseline population risk.
incorrectas.C: Hispanic women have an intermediate risk profile that is not highlighted as the peak-incidence demographic in classic fibroid epidemiology, unlike the clearly elevated risk documented in African American women.
incorrectas.D: Caucasian women have a lower incidence and typically later average age of fibroid diagnosis compared to African American women, making this the wrong demographic for the peak 20-40 year presentation described.

preguntas.q: A benign neoplastic proliferation of smooth muscle arising from the myometrium is best described as which entity (distinct from a proliferation of endometrium within the myometrium, which is called adenomyosis)?

e.correcta: A leiomyoma is a benign, well-circumscribed, whorled tumor of smooth muscle cells arising from and confined to the myometrium, growing under the influence of estrogen and progesterone and often regressing after menopause when hormone levels fall. This distinguishes it both from adenomyosis (ectopic endometrial glands/stroma within the myometrium, not a true neoplasm) and from its malignant counterpart, leiomyosarcoma, which shows necrosis, high mitotic activity, and infiltrative borders.

incorrectas.A: An endometrial polyp is a localized overgrowth of endometrial glands and stroma projecting into the uterine cavity, arising from the endometrial lining itself rather than being a smooth muscle proliferation from the myometrium.
incorrectas.C: Leiomyosarcoma is the malignant counterpart of leiomyoma, showing cytologic atypia, high mitotic rate, and tumor necrosis, and typically arises de novo in postmenopausal women rather than representing a benign myometrial smooth muscle growth.
incorrectas.D: Endometrial stromal sarcoma is a malignant tumor of endometrial stromal cells (not smooth muscle) that infiltrates the myometrium, making it a different cell lineage and a different (malignant) behavior than the benign leiomyoma described.

preguntas.q: Leiomyoma (uterine fibroid) growth is most directly related to exposure to which hormone?

e.correcta: Leiomyomas are benign smooth muscle tumors of the myometrium that are estrogen (and progesterone) sensitive — they typically enlarge during periods of high estrogen exposure (reproductive years, pregnancy) and regress after menopause when estrogen levels fall, reflecting estrogen receptor-driven proliferative signaling in the tumor cells. This hormone dependence underlies medical therapies (e.g., GnRH agonists) that induce a hypoestrogenic state to shrink fibroids before surgery.

incorrectas.B: Cortisol is a glucocorticoid involved in stress response and metabolism, with no established role in driving leiomyoma growth, which is governed by sex steroid signaling instead.
incorrectas.C: Testosterone is the principal androgen relevant to male physiology and virilization; it is not the hormone responsible for the growth pattern of estrogen-sensitive uterine fibroids.
incorrectas.D: Prolactin regulates lactation and is elevated in prolactinomas, but it is not the hormone implicated in leiomyoma growth, which correlates with estrogen exposure rather than prolactin levels.

preguntas.q: Because leiomyomas (fibroids) are estrogen-sensitive tumors, during which physiologic state would they be expected to increase in size, and during which would they be expected to decrease?

o.A: Increase with menopause; decrease with pregnancy
o.B: Increase with pregnancy; decrease with menopause
o.C: Increase with lactation; decrease with pregnancy
o.D: Increase with menopause; decrease with puberty

e.correcta: Leiomyomas are benign smooth muscle tumors whose growth is driven by estrogen (and progesterone) receptor signaling, so they tend to enlarge during pregnancy, when estrogen levels are markedly elevated, and shrink after menopause, when estrogen production falls dramatically. This hormone-responsiveness is exactly why fibroids are often followed conservatively through pregnancy (expecting growth) and why they are expected to regress once a woman becomes postmenopausal, sometimes reducing the need for surgical intervention.

incorrectas.A: This reverses the correct relationship — leiomyomas shrink, not grow, in the low-estrogen state of menopause, and grow, rather than shrink, during the high-estrogen state of pregnancy.
incorrectas.C: Lactation is typically associated with lower estrogen levels (due to prolactin-mediated suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis), so it would not be expected to increase fibroid size, and pregnancy is a high-estrogen state that increases rather than decreases fibroid size.
incorrectas.D: Puberty is a rising-estrogen state that would not be expected to shrink fibroids, and menopause causing growth is the opposite of what occurs — declining estrogen in menopause causes fibroid regression.

preguntas.q: Gross examination of a uterine mass reveals multiple, well-defined, white, whorled masses distorting the uterus and impinging on pelvic structures. What is the most likely diagnosis?

e.correcta: Leiomyomas (fibroids) are benign smooth muscle tumors of the myometrium that grossly appear as multiple, well-circumscribed, firm, white masses with a characteristic whorled cut surface, reflecting their origin from bundles of smooth muscle cells arranged in interlacing fascicles. Their well-defined borders (a pseudo-capsule of compressed surrounding myometrium) distinguish them grossly from more infiltrative or single, necrotic lesions.

incorrectas.A: Leiomyosarcoma, the malignant counterpart, is classically a single lesion with areas of necrosis and hemorrhage rather than multiple well-defined whorled masses, reflecting its more aggressive, infiltrative growth and outgrowing its blood supply.
incorrectas.B: Endometrial polyps are localized overgrowths of endometrial glands and stroma projecting into the uterine cavity, not firm, whorled myometrial masses distorting the uterine wall.
incorrectas.D: Endometrial carcinoma is a glandular epithelial malignancy typically presenting as an irregular, friable endometrial mass or diffuse thickening, not as multiple discrete, well-defined white whorled masses.

preguntas.q: What is the most common presentation of leiomyoma (fibroid), and if symptoms do occur, what is the most common symptom?

o.A: Usually causes infertility; when symptomatic, causes pelvic pain
o.B: Usually asymptomatic; when symptomatic, causes heavy menstrual bleeding
o.C: Usually causes constipation; when symptomatic, causes heavy menstrual bleeding
o.D: Usually causes heavy menstrual bleeding; when symptomatic, causes infertility

e.correcta: Most leiomyomas are small and asymptomatic, discovered incidentally on pelvic exam or imaging, because they do not necessarily distort the endometrial cavity or compress adjacent structures. When they do become symptomatic, the most common complaint is heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia), which occurs because the enlarged, irregular uterine cavity and altered vascular architecture impair normal endometrial hemostasis during shedding.

incorrectas.A: Infertility can occur with fibroids that distort the endometrial cavity or block tubal ostia, but this is not the most common presentation overall — most fibroids are asymptomatic, and heavy bleeding, not infertility, is the most common symptom when one does occur.
incorrectas.C: Constipation can result from a large fibroid compressing the rectum, but this is a less common presentation than asymptomatic incidental discovery, and heavy menstrual bleeding remains the most common symptom when fibroids do cause symptoms.
incorrectas.D: This reverses the correct hierarchy — heavy menstrual bleeding is the most common symptom when fibroids are symptomatic, while most fibroids are actually asymptomatic rather than routinely causing heavy bleeding as a default presentation.

preguntas.q: Severe or chronic bleeding caused by a leiomyoma (fibroid) may lead to which hematologic complication?

e.correcta: Chronic or heavy menstrual blood loss from a leiomyoma depletes the body's iron stores faster than dietary intake and marrow recycling can replace them, since each milliliter of blood lost contains iron bound in hemoglobin. This leads to a microcytic, hypochromic iron deficiency anemia, which is why women with heavy fibroid-related bleeding often present with fatigue, pallor, and low ferritin/low MCV on labs.

incorrectas.B: Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia is macrocytic and caused by impaired B12 absorption or intake (e.g., pernicious anemia, ileal disease), not by blood loss, so it would not result from fibroid-related menstrual bleeding.
incorrectas.C: Aplastic anemia results from bone marrow failure (e.g., toxin exposure, autoimmune destruction of stem cells), not from external blood loss, and is unrelated to the mechanism of fibroid-associated bleeding.
incorrectas.D: Hemolytic anemia results from premature destruction of red blood cells (intrinsic or extrinsic to the cell), not from blood loss through the uterus, so it does not describe the anemia caused by heavy fibroid bleeding.

preguntas.q: A postmenopausal woman is found to have a malignant proliferation of smooth muscle arising from the myometrium. What is this tumor called?

e.correcta: Leiomyosarcoma is a malignant smooth muscle tumor arising from the myometrium, most commonly in postmenopausal women, and unlike its benign counterpart it invades surrounding tissue, shows high mitotic activity, cellular atypia, and necrosis, and has metastatic potential (commonly to the lungs). Its aggressive behavior and de novo origin (not from a preexisting leiomyoma) make it clinically important to distinguish from benign fibroids, especially when a uterine mass grows rapidly after menopause when fibroids would typically be shrinking.

incorrectas.A: Leiomyoma is the benign counterpart — a smooth muscle tumor without invasive or metastatic potential — and would not be described as malignant.
incorrectas.B: Adenomyosis is the presence of endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium, a benign condition causing an enlarged, boggy uterus, not a malignant smooth muscle proliferation.
incorrectas.D: Endometrial stromal sarcoma arises from endometrial stromal cells, not smooth muscle, so while also malignant, it is a histologically and cell-of-origin distinct entity from the smooth muscle tumor described here.

preguntas.q: What is the precursor lesion for uterine leiomyosarcoma?

o.C: None; it arises de novo and does not develop from leiomyoma

e.correcta: Leiomyosarcoma is understood to arise de novo directly from myometrial smooth muscle cells rather than through malignant transformation of a preexisting benign leiomyoma — genetic and epidemiologic studies show these are molecularly distinct entities, not a progression sequence. This is clinically important because it means the presence of benign fibroids does not put a patient at increased risk of developing leiomyosarcoma, and a rapidly growing 'fibroid' (especially postmenopausally) should raise suspicion for a new, independent malignant process rather than degeneration of an existing one.

incorrectas.A: Leiomyoma is not a precursor lesion to leiomyosarcoma — despite the similar name, these are considered separate, unrelated entities rather than a stepwise progression like hyperplasia to carcinoma in the endometrium.
incorrectas.B: Endometrial hyperplasia is a glandular epithelial precursor lesion relevant to endometrial carcinoma, not to smooth muscle tumors like leiomyosarcoma, which arises from the myometrium rather than the endometrial glands.
incorrectas.D: Adenomyosis involves ectopic endometrial glands within the myometrium and is a benign, unrelated condition; it is not a precursor to the smooth muscle malignancy leiomyosarcoma.

preguntas.q: Gross examination of the uterus reveals a single lesion with areas of necrosis and hemorrhage. This finding is most consistent with which diagnosis (as opposed to multiple, well-defined, white, whorled masses)?

e.correcta: A single mass with necrosis and hemorrhage reflects the rapid, disorganized growth of a malignant tumor that outstrips its blood supply, causing areas of tissue death and bleeding within the mass — a gross hallmark of leiomyosarcoma. This contrasts sharply with the multiple, well-circumscribed, whorled white masses of benign leiomyoma, making gross appearance a useful (though not definitive) clue to malignancy that should prompt histologic evaluation for mitotic rate and atypia.

incorrectas.A: Leiomyoma classically presents as multiple, well-defined, white, whorled masses without necrosis or hemorrhage, which is the exact appearance the question contrasts against, making it the wrong answer here.
incorrectas.C: Endometrial polyps are localized endometrial overgrowths projecting into the uterine cavity, not myometrial masses with necrosis and hemorrhage, and lack the aggressive gross features described.
incorrectas.D: Adenomyosis produces a diffusely enlarged, boggy, trabeculated uterus from endometrial glands within the myometrium, not a single necrotic and hemorrhagic mass.

preguntas.q: An ovarian follicle consists of an oocyte surrounded by which two supporting cell types?

o.C: Cumulus and corona radiata cells only

e.correcta: An ovarian follicle consists of the oocyte surrounded by granulosa cells (which line the follicle, produce estrogen via aromatization, and respond to FSH) and an outer layer of theca cells (which respond to LH by producing androgens that granulosa cells then convert to estrogen). This two-cell, two-gonadotropin model is fundamental to understanding ovarian steroidogenesis and follicular maturation throughout the menstrual cycle.

incorrectas.A: Sertoli and Leydig cells are the analogous supporting cells in the testis (Sertoli cells nurture developing sperm and respond to FSH, Leydig cells produce testosterone in response to LH), not structures found within the ovarian follicle.
incorrectas.C: Cumulus and corona radiata cells are specialized subsets of granulosa cells that directly surround the oocyte and are extruded with it at ovulation, but they do not represent the complete set of supporting cell types in the follicle, which also requires the outer theca cell layer.
incorrectas.D: Stromal and hilus cells are ovarian interstitial cell types (hilus cells resemble Leydig cells and can secrete androgens) but are not the two defining cell types that constitute the structure of a developing follicle.

preguntas.q: Hemorrhage into a corpus luteum, especially during early pregnancy, can result in which type of ovarian cyst?

e.correcta: The corpus luteum is a highly vascularized structure that forms from the ruptured follicle after ovulation to produce progesterone supporting early pregnancy, and this rich vascularity makes it prone to spontaneous hemorrhage, particularly as it is further stimulated by rising hCG in early pregnancy. Bleeding into the corpus luteum forms a hemorrhagic corpus luteal cyst, which can cause acute pelvic pain and, if it ruptures, intraperitoneal bleeding requiring clinical attention.

incorrectas.A: A follicular cyst arises from a follicle that fails to rupture and ovulate, leading to fluid accumulation, a distinct mechanism from hemorrhage into an already-formed, ovulated corpus luteum.
incorrectas.C: An endometrioma is a cystic collection of ectopic endometrial tissue within the ovary (a 'chocolate cyst') related to endometriosis, not to hemorrhage within a corpus luteum.
incorrectas.D: A theca lutein cyst results from excessive gonadotropin (hCG) stimulation of theca cells, classically seen with molar pregnancy or multiple gestation, rather than from hemorrhage into a corpus luteum.

preguntas.q: Degeneration of ovarian follicles may result in which common, usually clinically insignificant, finding?

e.correcta: Follicular cysts are extremely common, benign findings that occur when a dominant ovarian follicle fails to rupture during ovulation, or when an atretic follicle degenerates and fluid accumulates within it — they are usually asymptomatic, small, and resolve spontaneously over a few menstrual cycles, making them a normal physiologic variant rather than a pathologic entity requiring intervention. Recognizing them as benign and self-limited on ultrasound helps avoid unnecessary surgical workup in most patients.

incorrectas.B: Endometriomas ('chocolate cysts') form when ectopic endometrial tissue implants on the ovary as part of endometriosis and undergoes cyclic bleeding, a distinct pathologic process related to retrograde menstruation rather than simple follicular degeneration.
incorrectas.C: Theca lutein cysts arise from excessive hCG stimulation of the theca cells, classically seen with molar pregnancies, choriocarcinoma, or multiple gestations/ovulation induction — a hormonally-driven process distinct from routine follicular atresia.
incorrectas.D: Serous cystadenomas are benign ovarian neoplasms arising from the surface epithelium, representing true tumor growth rather than a self-limited degenerative change of a normal follicle.

preguntas.q: A young woman presents with multiple follicular cysts in the ovary and anovulation due to a hormonal imbalance. What is this classically named condition?

e.correcta: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (Stein-Leventhal syndrome) results from a hormonal imbalance involving elevated LH relative to FSH and insulin resistance, which drives excess ovarian androgen production; this disrupts normal follicular maturation so that many follicles begin developing but fail to reach ovulation, arresting as multiple small follicular cysts and causing chronic anovulation. This combination of hyperandrogenism, anovulation, and polycystic ovaries explains the classic clinical triad of irregular menses, hirsutism/acne, and infertility seen in these patients.

incorrectas.A: Asherman syndrome is caused by intrauterine adhesions/scarring, usually from prior uterine instrumentation, leading to amenorrhea and infertility from a scarred endometrial cavity, not from ovarian follicular cysts or hormonal anovulation.
incorrectas.C: Turner syndrome (45,XO) causes ovarian dysgenesis with streak gonads and primary amenorrhea due to accelerated follicular atresia, not multiple follicular cysts from anovulation.
incorrectas.D: Sheehan syndrome is postpartum pituitary infarction due to hemorrhage-related hypotension, causing panhypopituitarism, which is unrelated to the ovarian follicular cyst formation and hyperandrogenism described in PCOS.

preguntas.q: In polycystic ovarian syndrome, what is the characteristic pattern of LH and FSH levels?

e.correcta: PCOS is driven by dysregulated GnRH pulsatility with an increased frequency of pulses, which preferentially stimulates pituitary LH synthesis/release over FSH, producing a high LH with a relatively low-normal FSH. The elevated LH drives ovarian theca cells to overproduce androgens, which are peripherally aromatized to estrone and also cause the hirsutism/acne seen clinically, while the low FSH impairs normal follicular maturation, contributing to anovulation and the classic 'string of pearls' cysts.

incorrectas.A: Low LH with high FSH is the pattern of primary ovarian insufficiency/menopause, where a failing ovary produces little estrogen/inhibin and the pituitary responds with unopposed elevation of both gonadotropins, especially FSH — the opposite direction of the gonadotropin skew seen in PCOS.
incorrectas.C: High LH with high FSH is not the characteristic pattern in PCOS; the defining feature is a discordant rise limited to LH, so an equal elevation of both hormones does not reflect the altered GnRH pulse frequency that selectively favors LH synthesis.
incorrectas.D: Low LH with low FSH would suggest hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (e.g., hypothalamic or pituitary failure, functional hypothalamic amenorrhea), which reflects reduced central drive to the gonadotropins rather than the altered pulsatility and LH-dominant pattern of PCOS.

preguntas.q: In polycystic ovarian syndrome, the LH:FSH ratio is often greater than what value?

e.correcta: The increased frequency of GnRH pulses in PCOS preferentially upregulates LH beta-subunit gene expression relative to FSH, so the LH:FSH ratio becomes skewed; a ratio greater than 2 (sometimes cited as >2-3) is a classic supportive laboratory finding, though it is neither required nor sufficient for diagnosis given the Rotterdam criteria's emphasis on clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism, oligo-anovulation, and polycystic ovarian morphology.

incorrectas.A: A ratio of 1 reflects a normal, roughly balanced LH:FSH relationship seen in eumenorrheic women outside of the LH surge, not the LH-dominant pattern characteristic of PCOS.
incorrectas.B: A ratio of 1.5 is still within the range that can be seen in normal cycling women and does not represent the degree of LH predominance classically used to support a PCOS pattern.
incorrectas.D: A ratio of 3 is higher than the classically cited threshold of 2; while some PCOS patients can have ratios this high or higher, the standard teaching point/threshold tested is greater than 2, not 3.

preguntas.q: Which demographic is most commonly affected by polycystic ovarian syndrome (Stein-Leventhal syndrome)?

o.D: Underweight women of advanced maternal age

e.correcta: PCOS classically presents in young, reproductive-age women, and obesity is a major contributor to its pathophysiology: excess adipose tissue drives peripheral insulin resistance and compensatory hyperinsulinemia, and insulin acts on theca cells (synergistically with LH) to increase ovarian androgen production while also suppressing hepatic SHBG synthesis, raising free testosterone. This combination of obesity, hyperandrogenism, and anovulation in young women is why Stein-Leventhal syndrome is taught as a disease of obese, young women.

incorrectas.A: Thin, adolescent girls are not the typical demographic — while PCOS can occur in lean patients, obesity is a well-recognized amplifier of the insulin-resistance-driven hyperandrogenism, making the 'thin' descriptor inconsistent with the classic presentation.
incorrectas.C: Postmenopausal women have declining ovarian follicular activity and low estrogen/androgen production overall; PCOS is fundamentally a disorder of anovulation during the reproductive years, so it does not present after menopause.
incorrectas.D: Underweight women of advanced maternal age fits neither the typical body habitus (obesity) nor the typical age group (young, reproductive-age, often in their 20s-30s at diagnosis) associated with PCOS.

preguntas.q: Polycystic ovarian syndrome is associated with which metabolic abnormality that may lead to type II diabetes mellitus 10-15 years later?

e.correcta: PCOS is strongly associated with insulin resistance, in which peripheral tissues (muscle, fat) respond poorly to insulin, prompting compensatory hyperinsulinemia; over time the pancreatic beta cells cannot indefinitely sustain this compensation, and impaired glucose tolerance progresses to overt type II diabetes mellitus in a substantial fraction of patients within about 10-15 years. This same hyperinsulinemia also drives ovarian androgen excess (via direct theca cell stimulation and reduced hepatic SHBG production), linking the reproductive and metabolic manifestations of PCOS to one shared mechanism.

incorrectas.B: Growth hormone deficiency is not a feature of PCOS and would produce short stature/metabolic derangements unrelated to hyperandrogenism or anovulation; PCOS pathophysiology centers on insulin resistance, not GH axis dysfunction.
incorrectas.C: Primary hyperaldosteronism causes hypertension and hypokalemia from excess mineralocorticoid activity, a distinct endocrine axis with no established mechanistic link to the hyperinsulinemia and hyperandrogenism seen in PCOS.
incorrectas.D: Hypothyroidism can cause menstrual irregularity and must be excluded when working up oligomenorrhea, but it is not the metabolic derangement inherent to PCOS pathophysiology or the one that predisposes to later type II diabetes.

preguntas.q: Patients with polycystic ovarian syndrome have an increased risk of which carcinoma, secondary to unopposed estrogen effects from chronic anovulation?

e.correcta: In PCOS, chronic anovulation means no corpus luteum forms and thus no progesterone is produced to oppose estrogen's proliferative effect on the endometrium; peripheral aromatization of the excess ovarian/adrenal androgens further adds to circulating estrogen. This unopposed estrogen drives continuous endometrial proliferation without the secretory transformation and shedding that progesterone normally provides, predisposing to endometrial hyperplasia and, over time, endometrial carcinoma.

incorrectas.A: Cervical carcinoma is driven predominantly by high-risk HPV infection causing dysplastic transformation of cervical epithelium, a mechanism unrelated to the anovulatory, estrogen-unopposed endometrial proliferation seen in PCOS.
incorrectas.C: Vaginal carcinoma is also generally HPV-related (or, rarely, associated with in-utero DES exposure for clear cell variants), and has no established mechanistic connection to chronic anovulation or unopposed estrogen in PCOS.
incorrectas.D: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is more classically associated with endometriosis, not with the unopposed-estrogen state of chronic anovulation; the tissue at risk from unopposed estrogen in PCOS is the endometrium, not the ovarian surface epithelium giving rise to clear cell tumors.

preguntas.q: What is the most common ovarian mass in young women?

e.correcta: Follicular cysts arise from the normal ovulatory cycle when a dominant graafian follicle fails to rupture (or ruptures and then reseals) and continues to accumulate follicular fluid, distending beyond its usual size; because this is simply an exaggeration of a routine physiologic event, follicular cysts are extremely common and represent the most frequent ovarian mass in young, reproductive-age women. They are typically thin-walled, lined by granulosa cells, and resolve spontaneously over one to a few menstrual cycles.

incorrectas.A: Serous cystadenoma is a true benign neoplasm arising from surface (coelomic) epithelium and, while common among ovarian tumors, is far less frequent overall in young women than the simple functional follicular cyst, which arises from routine follicular physiology rather than neoplastic proliferation.
incorrectas.C: Corpus luteal cysts form after ovulation when the corpus luteum fails to regress or bleeds into itself, but they are less common than follicular cysts, which form even before ovulation occurs and thus represent a more frequent overall category of functional ovarian mass.
incorrectas.D: Mucinous cystadenoma, like serous cystadenoma, is a true epithelial neoplasm and is considerably less common than a functional follicular cyst; neoplastic surface epithelial tumors are not the typical explanation for an ovarian mass in a young, otherwise healthy woman.

preguntas.q: A distention of an unruptured graafian follicle describes which type of ovarian cyst?

e.correcta: A follicular cyst is defined by distention of an unruptured graafian (dominant) follicle that continues to fill with fluid instead of rupturing to release the oocyte at ovulation. This purely mechanical/physiologic exaggeration — rather than a distinct pathologic or neoplastic process — is why follicular cysts are benign, typically small, and self-resolving over subsequent cycles.

incorrectas.A: A corpus luteal cyst forms after ovulation has already occurred, when the corpus luteum (formed from the ruptured follicle) either fails to involute normally or hemorrhages into itself — a distention of a post-ovulatory structure, not of the still-intact, unruptured follicle described here.
incorrectas.C: A theca lutein cyst results from excessive stimulation of theca cells by very high beta-hCG levels (e.g., in molar pregnancy or multiple gestation), producing luteinized cysts, which is a hormonally driven process distinct from simple mechanical distention of a normal unruptured follicle.
incorrectas.D: An endometrioma is a cystic collection of ectopic endometrial tissue and old hemorrhage within the ovary (a 'chocolate cyst'), arising from endometriosis rather than from the normal ovulatory follicle itself.

preguntas.q: Ovarian tumors may arise from three different cell types. Which of the following is NOT one of these three primary cell-of-origin categories?

e.correcta: Ovarian neoplasms are classically classified by cell of origin into three groups: surface (coelomic) epithelium, germ cells, and sex cord-stromal tissue, each reflecting a different embryologic/histologic component of the ovary and each giving rise to a characteristic set of tumors (e.g., serous/mucinous tumors from epithelium, teratomas/dysgerminomas from germ cells, granulosa/Sertoli-Leydig tumors from sex cord-stroma). Endometrial stromal cells are not a native ovarian cell population, so they are not one of these three foundational categories, even though endometrioid tumors can histologically resemble endometrial glands.

incorrectas.A: Surface epithelium is one of the three classic categories, giving rise to the most common ovarian tumors overall (serous, mucinous, endometrioid, Brenner, clear cell), so it is a correct category and not the answer being sought.
incorrectas.B: Germ cells are one of the three classic categories, producing tumors such as teratomas, dysgerminomas, and yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumors, particularly in younger patients, so this is also a valid category rather than the exception.
incorrectas.C: Sex cord-stromal tissue is the third classic category, giving rise to hormonally active tumors like granulosa cell tumors and Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors, and is therefore a legitimate cell-of-origin group, not the odd one out.

preguntas.q: Which class of ovarian tumor is the most common overall, accounting for approximately 70% of ovarian tumors?

e.correcta: Surface epithelial tumors arise from the coelomic (mesothelial-derived) epithelium covering the ovary, which has broad metaplastic potential to differentiate along serous (tubal), mucinous (endocervical/intestinal), or endometrioid lines. Because this epithelium is abundant and prone to neoplastic transformation with age, surface epithelial tumors are by far the most common category, accounting for roughly 65-70% of all ovarian tumors and the large majority of ovarian cancers in adult women.

incorrectas.A: Germ cell tumors are common in younger women (teens to 20s) but represent a much smaller overall share of ovarian tumors across all ages compared to surface epithelial tumors, which dominate numerically especially in older women.
incorrectas.B: Sex cord-stromal tumors are a distinct, less common category defined by hormonally active cells (granulosa, theca, Sertoli, Leydig) and make up a minority of ovarian tumors, far below the ~70% attributed to surface epithelial tumors.
incorrectas.D: Metastatic tumors to the ovary (e.g., Krukenberg tumors from gastric primaries) do occur but represent a smaller fraction of ovarian masses overall compared to primary surface epithelial neoplasms.

preguntas.q: Surface epithelial tumors of the ovary are derived embryologically from which type of epithelium that lines the ovary?

e.correcta: The ovary is covered by a single layer of coelomic (mesothelial) epithelium, embryologically derived from the same coelomic lining that also gives rise to the müllerian (paramesonephric) ducts; this shared origin explains why surface epithelial tumors can differentiate to resemble fallopian tube (serous), endocervical/intestinal (mucinous), or endometrial (endometrioid) tissue, mimicking the various müllerian-derived structures. This embryologic versatility of coelomic epithelium is the basis for the diverse histologic subtypes seen within the surface epithelial tumor category.

incorrectas.A: Mesonephric epithelium contributes to structures like the epididymis and vas deferens in males (and vestigial remnants in females, e.g., Gartner duct cysts), not to the surface lining of the ovary itself.
incorrectas.C: Urogenital sinus epithelium gives rise to the lower vagina and bladder, an embryologically distinct origin from the coelomic epithelium that covers the ovary and generates surface epithelial tumors.
incorrectas.D: Paramesonephric (müllerian) duct epithelium forms the fallopian tubes, uterus, and upper vagina, but the ovarian surface tumors arise from the adjacent coelomic epithelium covering the ovary itself, which secondarily differentiates to resemble müllerian tissue rather than arising directly from the ducts.

preguntas.q: What are the two most common subtypes of ovarian surface epithelial tumors, both of which are usually cystic?

e.correcta: Serous and mucinous tumors are the two most common subtypes of surface epithelial tumors because they reflect the coelomic epithelium's most frequent metaplastic differentiation pathways — serous tumors mimic fallopian tube epithelium and mucinous tumors mimic endocervical/intestinal mucin-producing epithelium. Both typically present as cystic masses (cystadenomas when benign), which is why they are grouped together as the dominant, usually-cystic subtypes compared to the less common endometrioid, clear cell, and Brenner tumors.

incorrectas.B: Endometrioid and clear cell tumors are real surface epithelial subtypes and are more often associated with endometriosis, but together they are less common than serous and mucinous tumors and are not the two dominant, usually-cystic subtypes being described.
incorrectas.C: Brenner and transitional cell tumors are rare surface epithelial tumors composed of urothelial-like (transitional) epithelium; they are notably more often solid than cystic and are far less common than serous/mucinous tumors.
incorrectas.D: Serous and Brenner pairs one of the two most common subtypes (serous) with one of the rarer, typically solid subtypes (Brenner), so this combination does not correctly identify the two most common, usually-cystic tumor types.

preguntas.q: A benign ovarian tumor composed of a single cyst with a simple, flat lining of epithelial cells is best classified as which entity?

e.correcta: A cystadenoma is, by definition, a benign glandular neoplasm forming a cyst lined by a single, simple (non-atypical) layer of epithelial cells without stromal invasion — reflecting benign proliferation of the surface epithelium rather than malignant transformation. This straightforward morphology (simple lining, no invasion, no complex papillary architecture) is what distinguishes it from its malignant counterpart, cystadenocarcinoma, and from borderline tumors that show some epithelial complexity/atypia but no invasion.

incorrectas.B: Cystadenocarcinoma is the malignant counterpart, characterized by a complex, shaggy, atypical epithelial lining with frank stromal invasion — the opposite of the simple, flat, benign lining described in the question.
incorrectas.C: Dermoid cyst (mature teratoma) is a germ cell tumor composed of multiple mature tissue types from different germ layers (skin, hair, teeth, etc.), not a single cyst with a simple epithelial lining derived from surface epithelium.
incorrectas.D: Fibroma is a solid sex cord-stromal tumor composed of spindle-shaped fibroblasts producing collagen, not a cystic lesion at all, so it does not match the single-cyst, simple-epithelial-lining description.

preguntas.q: Ovarian cystadenomas (surface epithelial tumors) most commonly arise in premenopausal women within which age range?

e.correcta: Ovarian cystadenomas, arising from proliferation of the surface (coelomic) epithelium, most commonly present in women during their 30s-40s — a period of ongoing ovulatory cycling and epithelial turnover on the ovarian surface that increases the opportunity for benign neoplastic change, well before the age range typically associated with malignant epithelial tumors, which trend older. This age distribution helps distinguish benign cystadenomas from cystadenocarcinomas, which more often present in postmenopausal women.

incorrectas.A: 10-20 years old is more typical of germ cell tumors (e.g., teratomas, dysgerminomas), not surface epithelial cystadenomas, which require years of epithelial exposure/turnover and are uncommon in adolescents.
incorrectas.C: 50-60 years old is an age range more associated with malignant surface epithelial tumors (cystadenocarcinomas), which tend to present later in life than the benign cystadenomas described in the question.
incorrectas.D: 70-80 years old is well beyond the typical presentation window for benign cystadenomas and is more consistent with advanced-stage malignant epithelial ovarian cancer, which is diagnosed disproportionately in older postmenopausal women.

preguntas.q: What is the most common benign ovarian tumor, classically lined with fallopian tube-like epithelium and often bilateral?

e.correcta: Serous cystadenoma is the most common benign ovarian tumor overall; it arises when coelomic surface epithelium differentiates along a serous (fallopian-tube-like) lineage, producing a thin-walled cyst lined by ciliated, tubal-type epithelium. Bilaterality is relatively frequent (roughly 20-25% of cases) compared to other epithelial tumors, a feature useful for distinguishing it on imaging or at surgery.

incorrectas.A: Mucinous cystadenoma is also a common benign epithelial tumor, but it is lined by mucin-secreting, endocervical/intestinal-type epithelium rather than fallopian-tube-like epithelium, and it is typically unilateral and often larger/multiloculated — distinguishing it from the tubal-epithelium, frequently bilateral serous cystadenoma described here.
incorrectas.C: Brenner tumor is a much rarer surface epithelial tumor composed of solid nests of transitional (urothelial-like) epithelium, not the tubal-type lining or the frequent bilaterality that characterizes serous cystadenoma.
incorrectas.D: Mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) is a germ cell tumor containing multiple tissue types from different germ layers (skin, hair, teeth), not a surface epithelial tumor lined by fallopian-tube-like epithelium.

preguntas.q: A benign ovarian cystic tumor is lined by fallopian tube-like (tubal) epithelium and is often bilateral. Which surface epithelial tumor is this?

e.correcta: Serous cystadenoma is lined by ciliated, fallopian tube-like (tubal) epithelium because the coelomic surface epithelium of the ovary differentiates along the serous lineage, recapitulating the müllerian tubal phenotype; it also has a notably higher rate of bilaterality than other benign epithelial tumors. These two features together (tubal-type lining plus frequent bilaterality) are the classic identifying combination tested for serous cystadenoma.

incorrectas.A: Mucinous cystadenoma is lined by mucin-producing, endocervical or intestinal-type epithelium rather than tubal epithelium, and it is characteristically unilateral, unlike the bilateral, tubal-lined tumor described in the question.
incorrectas.C: Brenner tumor consists of solid nests of transitional (urothelial-like) epithelium with characteristic 'coffee bean' grooved nuclei, not a cystic tumor lined by ciliated tubal epithelium.
incorrectas.D: Endometrioid tumor is lined by glands resembling endometrial tissue (often associated with endometriosis) rather than fallopian tube-like epithelium, and it is more frequently malignant than benign, unlike the benign, tubal-lined tumor being described.

preguntas.q: An ovarian tumor shows complex cysts with a shaggy epithelial lining and frank invasion into the underlying connective tissue/stroma. What is this lesion?

e.correcta: Cystadenocarcinoma is the malignant counterpart of the serous/mucinous cystadenoma spectrum, defined histologically by a complex, shaggy (papillary, architecturally disorganized) epithelial lining together with frank invasion of the tumor cells into the underlying stroma. This invasive growth is the key feature that distinguishes true carcinoma from a benign cystadenoma (simple, flat lining, no invasion) and from a borderline tumor (epithelial complexity/atypia present but no destructive stromal invasion).

incorrectas.A: Serous cystadenoma is the benign form with a simple, flat, non-atypical epithelial lining and no invasion into the stroma — the opposite of the complex, invasive picture described in the question.
incorrectas.B: Borderline serous tumor shows increased epithelial complexity and cellular atypia compared to a benign cystadenoma, but by definition it lacks destructive stromal invasion, which is precisely the feature present in the case described, making cystadenocarcinoma the better fit.
incorrectas.D: Cystic teratoma is a germ cell tumor containing multiple mature tissue types (skin, hair, teeth) rather than a surface epithelial lesion, and it does not typically show a shaggy epithelial lining with stromal invasion, which is a surface-epithelial-carcinoma feature.

preguntas.q: Malignant ovarian surface epithelial tumors (adenocarcinomas) most commonly arise in women of which age group?

e.correcta: Malignant ovarian surface epithelial tumors (like serous and mucinous cystadenocarcinoma) most commonly arise in women aged 60-70, reflecting the cumulative effect of decades of ovulatory cycles causing repeated surface epithelial disruption and repair, which increases the chance of accumulating oncogenic mutations (the 'incessant ovulation' hypothesis). This age distribution, along with risk factors like nulliparity and BRCA mutations that increase lifetime ovulation exposure, helps explain why epithelial ovarian cancer risk rises steadily with age unlike germ cell tumors, which peak in younger women.

incorrectas.A: 15-30 years old is the age range more typical of germ cell tumors like dysgerminoma, not epithelial ovarian adenocarcinoma, which requires many years of cumulative ovulatory epithelial damage to develop.
incorrectas.B: 30-40 years old is still relatively early for epithelial ovarian malignancy; benign epithelial tumors (like serous cystadenoma) are more common in this younger range, while malignant transformation typically requires more time.
incorrectas.D: 40-50 years old is an intermediate age at which epithelial ovarian tumors can occur but is not the peak incidence; the classic teaching point is that malignant epithelial ovarian tumors peak later, in the 60-70 age range.

preguntas.q: Ovarian tumors with epithelial features intermediate between clearly benign and clearly malignant are classified as which category?

e.correcta: Borderline tumors (tumors of low malignant potential) show epithelial proliferation, cytologic atypia, and increased mitoses that exceed benign cystadenomas but, critically, lack destructive stromal invasion, placing them in an intermediate category between clearly benign and clearly malignant lesions. This distinction matters clinically because borderline tumors have a much better prognosis than invasive carcinoma even when they spread beyond the ovary, since true stromal invasion—the histologic hallmark of malignancy—is absent.

incorrectas.A: Cystadenocarcinoma is the fully malignant, invasive counterpart of ovarian epithelial tumors, showing frank stromal invasion, which is precisely the feature separating it from the intermediate borderline category described.
incorrectas.C: Cystadenoma is the benign end of the spectrum, showing bland, simple epithelium without the epithelial atypia and proliferation seen in borderline tumors.
incorrectas.D: Brenner tumor is a distinct histologic subtype of ovarian epithelial tumor composed of transitional (urothelial-like) epithelium, usually benign, and is not itself the name for the intermediate malignant-potential category being asked about.

preguntas.q: Compared to clearly malignant ovarian carcinomas, borderline ovarian tumors are best characterized by which combination of features?

o.A: Worse prognosis and no metastatic potential
o.B: Better prognosis and no metastatic potential
o.C: Better prognosis but retain some metastatic potential
o.D: Equivalent prognosis and equivalent metastatic potential

e.correcta: Borderline ovarian tumors show epithelial proliferation and cytologic atypia intermediate between benign cystadenomas and frank carcinomas, but crucially lack destructive stromal invasion; this absence of true invasion is why they behave less aggressively and carry a better prognosis than invasive carcinoma, yet they can still implant on peritoneal surfaces or rarely recur/spread, meaning they are not entirely without metastatic-like potential the way a purely benign tumor is.

incorrectas.A: Worse prognosis and no metastatic potential is internally inconsistent with how borderline tumors actually behave — their prognosis is better than carcinoma precisely because they lack destructive invasion, even though limited spread (e.g., peritoneal implants) can still occur.
incorrectas.B: Better prognosis and no metastatic potential correctly captures the improved prognosis but overstates the case by denying any spread potential; borderline tumors can still produce peritoneal implants or, rarely, recur, so 'no metastatic potential' is too absolute.
incorrectas.D: Equivalent prognosis and equivalent metastatic potential ignores the entire point of the borderline category, which exists specifically because these tumors behave less aggressively than fully invasive carcinomas despite sharing some cytologic atypia.

preguntas.q: A postmenopausal woman is found to have a bilateral ovarian mass with psammoma bodies on histology. Which is the most common malignant ovarian neoplasm overall?

e.correcta: Serous cystadenocarcinoma is the most common malignant ovarian neoplasm overall, reflecting the fact that surface epithelial tumors as a class dominate ovarian neoplasia and that the serous subtype is the most frequent within that group. Psammoma bodies — concentric, laminated calcifications thought to form around foci of necrotic tumor cell debris — are a classic histologic clue for serous tumors (both benign and malignant), and bilaterality is also common in this subtype, both features matching the vignette.

incorrectas.B: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma is less common than the serous subtype and is not classically associated with psammoma bodies, which are a hallmark specifically of serous (and papillary thyroid/meningioma) histology rather than mucinous tumors.
incorrectas.C: Granulosa cell tumor is a sex cord-stromal tumor that classically produces estrogen (and can show Call-Exner bodies histologically), not psammoma bodies, and it is far less common overall than serous cystadenocarcinoma.
incorrectas.D: Dysgerminoma is a germ cell tumor most common in younger women, histologically resembling seminoma with sheets of cells and lymphocytic infiltrate, not psammoma bodies, and it is not the most common ovarian malignancy overall.

preguntas.q: A rare ovarian surface epithelial tumor composed of glands resembling endometrial tissue, usually malignant and sometimes linked to endometriosis, is best classified as which tumor type?

e.correcta: Endometrioid tumors are surface epithelial neoplasms whose glands histologically resemble normal endometrium, reflecting the coelomic epithelium's capacity for müllerian-type differentiation along an endometrial rather than tubal or mucinous line; unlike serous and mucinous tumors, endometrioid tumors are usually malignant at diagnosis and have a well-recognized association with pre-existing endometriosis, from which they can arise via malignant transformation of ectopic endometrial glands.

incorrectas.B: Serous tumors are lined by fallopian-tube-like (ciliated) epithelium rather than endometrial-gland-like epithelium, and while they can be malignant, they are not the subtype specifically linked to endometriosis in the way endometrioid tumors are.
incorrectas.C: Brenner tumor is composed of solid nests of transitional (urothelial-like) epithelium with grooved 'coffee bean' nuclei, morphologically and clinically distinct from the glandular, endometrium-like pattern and endometriosis association described here.
incorrectas.D: Mucinous tumors are lined by mucin-producing, endocervical/intestinal-type epithelium, not endometrial-gland-like epithelium, and they lack the characteristic association with endometriosis that defines endometrioid tumors.

preguntas.q: Approximately what percentage of ovarian endometrioid tumors are associated with a separate, independent primary endometrial (uterine) carcinoma?

e.correcta: About 15% of ovarian endometrioid carcinomas are associated with a synchronous, independent primary endometrial carcinoma, reflecting shared risk factors (unopposed estrogen exposure) and a shared histogenetic pathway from endometriosis or Müllerian metaplasia rather than one lesion metastasizing from the other. This distinction matters clinically because molecular/clonality studies are sometimes used to confirm these are two separate primaries rather than a single metastatic process, which changes staging and prognosis.

incorrectas.A: 50% substantially overstates the association; while endometrioid ovarian tumors do have a notable link to endometrial pathology, the commonly cited synchronous primary rate is around 15%, not one in two cases.
incorrectas.B: 5% understates the well-documented association between ovarian and endometrial endometrioid tumors, which is higher than this due to their shared estrogen-driven pathogenesis.
incorrectas.D: 30% overstates the frequency; this figure is higher than the accepted approximate rate of 15% cited for synchronous independent endometrial primaries in ovarian endometrioid tumors.

preguntas.q: A solid, encapsulated, yellow-tan ovarian tumor shows nuclei with a characteristic longitudinal groove on H&E, described as "coffee bean" nuclei. Which tumor is this?

e.correcta: Brenner tumor is a solid surface epithelial tumor composed of nests of transitional (urothelial-like) epithelium embedded in abundant fibrous stroma, giving it a firm, yellow-tan, encapsulated gross appearance; the epithelial cell nuclei classically show a longitudinal groove imparting a 'coffee bean' appearance, analogous to the nuclear grooves seen in urothelial cells. This distinctive nuclear morphology plus the solid, fibrous, usually benign nature is the key combination that identifies Brenner tumor.

incorrectas.B: Serous cystadenoma is a cystic tumor lined by ciliated, tubal-type epithelium, not a solid yellow-tan mass, and it does not show the characteristic coffee bean nuclear grooves seen in Brenner tumor.
incorrectas.C: Granulosa cell tumor is a sex cord-stromal tumor that is typically estrogen-secreting and shows Call-Exner bodies (small follicle-like structures) histologically, not the transitional epithelium and coffee bean nuclei characteristic of Brenner tumor.
incorrectas.D: Krukenberg tumor is a metastatic tumor (classically from gastric signet ring cell carcinoma) showing mucin-filled signet ring cells within ovarian stroma, an entirely different histologic picture from the solid, transitional-epithelium morphology with grooved nuclei seen in Brenner tumor.
